subject: Urgent: Solara Systems AZ1->AZ2 asymmetric errors; request for geo-failover
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@solara-systems.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Sep 2028 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: High 5xx spike + latency for AZ1 traffic - immediate help needed

Karthik / Redwood on-call,

We’re seeing a sharp uptick in 5xx errors and tail latency for requests served from AZ1 starting ~10:40 PT. The errors are largely correlated with longer requests (prompt lengths > 1k tokens) but we’re also seeing short-request failures. Customer impact: our payment processing flow is failing intermittently and several sessions have been dropped.

Key metrics attached (latency snapshot + raw error samples). Can you confirm whether Redwood can route traffic off AZ1 to AZ2 for Solara while we investigate? Our customers are transactional — we need a quick mitigation and an ETA for a regional fix.

Alex Turner
Head of Platform Ops
Solara Systems
ops@solara-systems.com

---
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@solara-systems.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Sep 2028 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx spike + latency for AZ1 traffic - immediate help needed

Alex — thanks for the heads up and attachments, we’re looking now. Initial quick answers:
- We can perform a targeted regional reroute for Solara from us-east-az1 -> us-east-az2 at the Redwood edge routing layer. That action is reversible.
- We’ll need a brief maintenance window (2–5 minutes) to shift weights and warm caches; there may be a small increase in token latency immediately after the shift while caches fill.

I’m escalating to Soojin (CS lead) and Marissa (solutions/infra) to coordinate the runbook steps and customer comms.

Planned next steps (30 min):
1) Confirm SLO tolerance and rollback conditions with Solara (Alex)
2) Mobilize infra runbook: start with read-only traffic split, then full steer if metrics stabilize
3) Open an exec bridge with Redwood leadership if we hit errors during failover

Will send an ETA for the failover in the next 10 minutes.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
From: soojin_lee@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@solara-systems.com>, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Sep 2028 11:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx spike + latency for AZ1 traffic - immediate help needed

Karthik / Marissa — I’ve pulled the customer SLA: Solara is on enterprise standing with a 99.9% regional availability SLA and a credit clause for sustained regional impact >30m. Customer tolerance: they want least-disruptive mitigation but will accept a geo-steer temporarily if it reduces errors.

I’ll draft the customer note once infra confirms the plan. Also cc’ing Sean for executive awareness and to scope any credit conversation if this extends.

Soojin Lee
Customer Success Manager, Redwood

---
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, Alex Turner <alex.turner@solara-systems.com>
Cc: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Sep 2028 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx spike + latency for AZ1 traffic - immediate help needed

Team — I’ve validated the infra signals. We’re seeing KV cache saturation on the AZ1 serving pool for the large context requests; kernel selection is falling back to a slower path and then hitting an OOM on edge pods, which manifests as 5xx.

Recommendation: perform a two-stage steer:
1) 10m read-only traffic split to AZ2 to validate no regressions (route 20% of sessions that are idempotent/read flows)
2) If stable, switch to 100% for up to 60 minutes while we collect a full heap/profile and rotate vulnerable pods.

I will kick off the playbook now and attach the playbook artifacts. Expect brief token-latency bump (50–150ms) immediately post-shift.

Attachments: geo_failover_playbook_v2.pdf, latency_snapshot_20280925.png, error_samples_0925.txt

— Marissa Cole
Principal Infra Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@solara-systems.com>
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Sep 2028 12:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx spike + latency for AZ1 traffic - immediate help needed

Alex— we’re ready to proceed with the two-stage steer. Please confirm acceptance of:
- 20% idempotent/read-only split for 10 minutes as a smoke test
- Fallback to 100% for up to 60 minutes if stable
- Expected transient token latency increase of ~100ms during warmup

If you approve, we’ll start the steering at 12:25 PT. Also note: if this extends >30 minutes of degraded availability, we’ll need to engage formal SLA credit review (Soojin).

Karthik

---
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@solara-systems.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: soojin_lee@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, sean_gallagher@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 25 Sep 2028 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx spike + latency for AZ1 traffic - immediate help needed

Karthik / team — please proceed. We approve the two-stage plan. Our priority is transactional correctness; the 100% failover window is acceptable. Please keep us updated every 10 minutes and include the expected post-mitigations timeline.

Alex

---
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Alex Turner <alex.turner@solara-systems.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Sep 2028 12:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High 5xx spike + latency for AZ1 traffic - immediate help needed

ACTION LOG:
12:25 PT — Initiated 20% idempotent split to us-east-az2 (read-only flows). Monitoring:
- 12:29 PT — no increase in errors for split traffic; latency stable (+50ms)
- 12:35 PT — warm cache metrics improving on AZ2; error rate for AZ1 holding ~2.8% (down from 7.6%)
12:40 PT — Proceeding to 100% steer to us-east-az2 for Solara.

12:45 PT — 100% traffic now on AZ2. Observed: 5xx rate dropped to 0.4% and tail latency returned near baseline after caches warmed (within ~120s).

Post-action plan: full heap/profile export on AZ1 pods, rotate pods with large contexts, follow-up incident report within 24 hours.

Marissa

---
From: sean_gallagher@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@solara-systems.com>
Date: Wed, 27 Sep 2028 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: Exec note and next steps for Solara AZ incident

Quick executive note:
- Customer impact was mitigated via geo-steer to AZ2; immediate business continuity achieved.
- Root cause (preliminary): KV cache saturation + kernel path fallback on AZ1 serving pool under heavy large-context reqs.
- Next steps: Marissa to own infra remediation (pod rotation + config guardrails). Soojin to coordinate SLA credit flow if Solara requests. Karthik to produce incident RCA and customer-facing summary by EOD today.

I’m available if Solara requests any executive-level concessions (credits / extended support) — advise and I’ll join any calls.

— Sean Gallagher
VP, Customer Success and GTM Operations, Redwood Inference
